Key agrees: analysis.key measured D minor. Instrumentation agrees with the brief's technical direction — the analysis names lead male vocals, backing vocals, electric guitar, distorted electric guitar, bass guitar, drums, drum machine and synth pads. The analysis labels the genre "Alternative Rock" while the brief's style reads "dark pastoral synthwave": the guitar-forward, dark-production half of the brief is attested, the synthwave half is not, and timbral and production texture remain not observable from the bundle.

The analysis' 6 sections match the brief's 6 declared sections and each boundary is within ~2 s of the declaration: Intro 00:00–00:11 (brief 0:00), Verse 1 00:11–00:47 (0:10), Chorus 1 00:47–01:14 (0:45), Verse 2 01:14–01:45 (1:15), Chorus 2 01:45–02:11 (1:45), Outro 02:11–02:29 (2:10). analysis.sections measured 6 against the brief's 6 structure entries (unit sections, source lyria instance analysis).

The bundle carries authored EN lyric text, tagged [Verse] / [Chorus] / [Outro] in the order the structure declares (two verses, two choruses, one outro), with consistent two-line shapes inside each section and no prose sentences in place of hook lines. Language matches the brief's EN. Mix-level intelligibility is not observable from the bundle and is not claimed.

A repeated hook line is locatable in the lyric text inside the declared chorus sections: "Wake me where the orchids grow" with its answering line appears in the [Chorus] block that the structure places at 0:45 and again at 1:45 (structure entries Chorus and Chorus). The bundle makes no claim about whether the melody is memorable.

No artefact is recorded as a row: silence.leading measured 0 s and silence.trailing 0.67 s, both pass (unit s, source ffmpeg 9.0.1 silencedetect), and no delivery rows exist yet because the take has not been mastered. Clipping, dropout, clicks and vocal-timbre artefacts are only audible and therefore unattested from the bundle.

feedback: Tempo is the one measured miss: the take rendered at 90 bpm against the brief's 150 BPM ask (analysis.bpm warn, source lyria instance analysis). A next iterate should state the tempo as the single dominant instruction at the start of `style` and drop the competing "wide choruses" framing from the same sentence, or accept the slower half-time reading deliberately and re-brief the structure timings to match it.
